prompt:
Paint ONE building for a top-down pixel-art JRPG town map, in the classic 3/4 top-down RPG view: the roof is seen from above (it fills the upper coloured block of the guide) and the front wall is seen straight on (the lower block). The attached image is an exact layout guide drawn at the final proportions: keep the outer silhouette, the roof/wall split line, the door (dark brown rectangle: it must stay exactly there, same size, at ground level, a real door you can walk through) and the windows (yellow rectangles) in exactly the same places. You may add small details (eaves, trim, drainpipe, flower boxes, crates by the wall, a chimney poking above the roof into the empty top margin).
This building: a one-storey house in a stone-and-plaster harbour town on a windy northern coast. blue-grey slate roof with overlapping slates and a ridge cream plaster walls with dark timber framing and a stone plinth. Windows have small panes glowing warm amber from inside (the only light). The whole image is 208 x 192 art pixels (each art pixel 7x7 image pixels).
Premium modern hi-bit 2D pixel art ("HD pixel art" JRPG look), hand-placed pixels. Every art pixel is a crisp square of the same size across the whole image (about 8x8 image pixels per art pixel). No anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft brushes, no photographic texture, no noise, no dithering checkerboards. Clusters of 3-10 pixels with clear shapes. Hue-shifted colour ramps: shadows lean toward purple/red and are more saturated, highlights lean toward warm yellow. 4-6 shades per material, rich but earthy, worn and lived-in.
Lighting: neutral, soft, even light from the upper left, like a calm overcast evening; NO cast shadows, NO night darkness, NO lamp light pools, NO vignette. (The game engine adds the night lighting on top later, so this must be the clean base colours.)
Background: fully transparent (the magenta in the guide is background). No ground, no shadow, no people, no text, no letters.
revised_prompt: Edit the attached layout-guide image into ONE standalone 3/4 top-down JRPG pixel-art house sprite. Treat the attached image as an EXACT tracing template, not a loose inspiration. Preserve the guide's outer silhouette and precise roof/wall dividing line; preserve the precise locations and sizes of BOTH yellow windows and the dark brown ground-level door (a genuine walk-through door, not a roof ornament); DO NOT move, delete, or resize any of these features. Roof fills the entire upper blue-grey guide block, shown from above as a broad rectangular blue-grey slate roof, with carefully clustered overlapping slate tiles, a subtle ridge, and a thin eave along its lower horizontal edge. The lower cream guide block is the straight-on front facade, cream plaster with dark timber framing and a worn stone plinth; put the warm amber small-paned glazing within each EXISTING window rectangle, and preserve the entrance at the guide's existing door rectangle. A modest stone chimney can rise into the blank top margin. One-storey harbour-town house on a windy northern coast, lived-in but restrained. High-end modern hi-bit JRPG pixel art; hand-placed crisp identically sized SQUARE pixels, artwork at 208 x 192 art pixels, scaled up by factor 7 with nearest-neighbor hard edges (no antialiasing or blur), economical pixel clusters of 3–10 pixels, hue-shifted 4–6 tone material ramps: purple-red saturated shadows and warm-yellow highlights. Calm evenly lit neutral overcast-evening BASE COLORS, with glowing window glass as the ONLY light; no night tint, no cast shadow, no pools of light, no vignette. Transparent alpha background in place of ALL the bright magenta guide color; no ground, no shadow, no figures or writing. Do not alter the sprite proportions or tilt the front facade into an isometric wall. Pixel-perfect alignment to attached guide is the priority.
